title: Foundations
description: What MATLAB is for, and the four ideas — variables, vectors, matrices, indexing — that everything else is built from.

project.title: Per-unit base converter
project.description: A working tool that converts impedances between base MVA and kV, validated against a hand calculation. Uses every idea in this module and nothing beyond it.

title: Programming
description: Scripts, functions, control flow and debugging — the point at which you stop typing commands and start building things that can be re-run.

project.title: Symmetrical fault current calculator
project.description: Takes a system base, a Thevenin impedance and a fault location, returns fault current and MVA. Structured as real functions with input validation.

title: Data and Visualisation
description: Reading real measurement files, and turning numbers into figures good enough for a report or a paper.

project.title: Daily load curve analyser
project.description: Reads a year of half-hourly load data, finds peak and minimum demand days, computes load factor, and produces a publication-quality figure.

title: Numerical Methods
description: Why the computer's answer differs from the maths answer, and how the solvers you'll rely on actually work.

project.title: Newton-Raphson from scratch
project.description: Implement the root-finding method by hand, watch it converge quadratically, and break it deliberately to see when it doesn't.

title: Engineering Toolboxes
description: Symbolic Math, Optimization, Control System, Signal Processing, Simulink and Simscape Electrical — what each is for and when to reach for it.

project.title: Transmission line parameter calculator
project.description: Derive ABCD parameters symbolically, then compute them numerically for a real line and compare short, medium and long line models.

title: Power System Applications
description: The payoff: Y-bus, load flow, symmetrical components, fault analysis and harmonics, written from first principles.

project.title: Complete load-flow tool
project.description: Newton-Raphson load flow with a simple GUI, validated against published IEEE 14-bus results. The point at which the coursework stops being intimidating.

title: Python Foundations
description: The language itself — types, collections, control flow, functions and the module system — for someone who already thinks in MATLAB.

project.title: Unit conversion library
project.description: A properly packaged module of electrical unit conversions, with tests. Your first thing that is code rather than a script.

title: NumPy
description: Arrays, broadcasting, and the mental shift from MATLAB's matrix-first world to NumPy's array-first one.

project.title: Y-bus builder, vectorised
project.description: Build an admittance matrix with no Python-level loops, then compare its speed against the loop version.

title: pandas
description: Time series done properly — indexing, resampling, timezones and the gap-handling that measurement data always needs.

project.title: Feeder measurement cleaner
project.description: Take a messy year of SCADA-style data with gaps and duplicates, and produce a clean hourly series you'd be willing to publish from.

title: Matplotlib
description: Figures for reports and papers, including the conventions specific to power systems — voltage profiles, duration curves, phasor diagrams.

title: Scientific Computing
description: SciPy's sparse matrices, linear solvers, optimisation and signal processing — the engine room for real studies.

project.title: Sparse load flow
project.description: Rebuild the load-flow solver using scipy.sparse and measure how the advantage grows with system size.

title: Power System Applications
description: pandapower and OpenDSS driven from Python, and the reproducibility discipline that makes a study trustworthy.

project.title: Automated hosting capacity study
project.description: Drive OpenDSS across hundreds of scenarios from Python, and report a penetration-violation curve rather than a single number.

title: From MATLAB to Python
description: A direct translation guide, written to be read last — once both languages are familiar enough for the differences to be interesting.
